title: Student Voice is Shocking
author: Dominic Salles
summary: A comprehensive national survey of student attitudes reveals significantly low engagement across five critical domains: safety, behavior, academic value, enjoyment, and peer relationships. The data comes from the ImpactEd student voice assessment, a 32-question instrument that measures cognitive engagement (whether students feel safe, perceive academic value, and exercise agency), emotional engagement (enjoyment, worry levels, and sense of belonging), and behavioral engagement (effort and persistence). The findings are sobering: average engagement scores lag well behind what educators would hope. Schools can use this benchmark tool to situate their own student populations, celebrate areas where they exceed national averages, and identify specific improvement targets grounded in evidence. The survey provides a diagnostic window into which dimensions of student experience are strongest and which require intervention.
points: National student data shows shockingly low average engagement across multiple dimensions of school experience
The ImpactEd questionnaire measures six key domains: pupil safety and behavior, value placed on education, academic agency, enjoyment and worry, inclusion and fairness, and peer relationships
Schools can use student voice data as a diagnostic tool to identify which engagement dimensions are weakest in their context
Disaggregated data by demographic groups reveals which students feel least safe, valued, and included
The baseline enables schools to set realistic improvement targets and track progress toward better student experiences
